style: Vincenzo Montella's fluid 4-2-3-1 with a loose, interchangeable front four. Hakan Calhanoglu and Ismail Yuksek provide the base, while Arda Guler roams to find pockets of space and technical forwards rotate freely. Possession-based and technically rich, built around young creators.
recent_form: Back at the World Cup for the first time since 2002 after a strong cycle under Montella (roughly 59% win rate). Buoyed by the rise of Guler and Yildiz; high expectations after reaching the Euro 2024 quarter-finals.

key_players.name: Hakan Calhanoglu
key_players.note: Inter Milan midfielder who controls tempo, sets the base of midfield and delivers set pieces.

key_players.name: Arda Guler
key_players.note: Real Madrid playmaker in exceptional 2025-26 form; given license to roam and create chances.

key_players.name: Kenan Yildiz
key_players.note: Juventus forward and one of Europe's most exciting young players; direct and incisive in the final third.

key_players.name: Merih Demiral
key_players.note: Experienced, aggressive centre-back anchoring the back line.

key_players.name: Kerem Akturkoglu
key_players.note: Pacey, goal-threat winger who rotates within the fluid front four.

key_players.name: Ferdi Kadioglu
key_players.note: Mobile full-back who provides width and overlaps to support the attack.

historical_news: Türkiye returns to the World Cup after a 24-year absence, last appearing in 2002 when they finished third.
Vincenzo Montella guided the team to qualification and to the Euro 2024 quarter-finals.
Young stars Arda Guler and Kenan Yildiz, neither born at Türkiye's last World Cup, headline a new generation.
Captain Hakan Calhanoglu provides veteran leadership for a youthful, attacking side.
Squad blends emerging talent with Serie A and European experience under Montella.

media_sentiment.label: positive
media_sentiment.summary: Excitement over a talented young generation and a long-awaited return to the World Cup, with optimism tempered by defensive consistency questions.
